subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw approve a bounded per-reviewer-instance exact-input cache for low-risk model-backed exec auto-review decisions while keeping approval state non-durable?
rationale: The source bug is narrow, but skipping a fresh model review for a later identical exec request changes approval-boundary semantics, so cache scope needs explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Cache only within the shared reviewer/run lifetime, key by the full reviewed input or prompt, keep allow-once non-durable, and require real configured-run proof before merge.

options.title: Require narrower cache semantics
options.body: Limit caching to parsed low-risk allow-once decisions or another stricter key/lifetime if maintainers want a smaller approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization for now and accept one reviewer completion per exec request to preserve one-request-one-review behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Cache only within the shared reviewer/run lifetime, key by the full reviewed input or prompt, keep allow-once non-durable, and require real configured-run proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the normalized exec auto-reviewer behavior and is the clearest owner-history signal for the approval-boundary semantics.
